(1) `scripts/i601_launch.sh:77` opens `$LOG_DIR/issue-601-smoke-results.json` with no `.processed` fallback. The sentinel is poll_pipeline-compliant (`_write_sentinel`, `dispatch_neg_setpoint_601.py:75-81`, `sentinel_schema_version: 1`), so the poller's drain (globs `issue-<N>-*.json`, posts the marker, renames to `.processed`) WILL rename it on any tick. The window is not trivial: the dispatcher writes the sentinel (`:538`) BEFORE the smoke raw-completions HF upload (`:550-558`), so it spans the whole upload plus uv startup. The margin co-read is the saturation-safe read that exists precisely because logp compresses near ceiling; mixing spaces corrupts its horizon/coupling/matched-pair verdicts in the pinned registered analysis output. That `arm_terminals_margin` was built separately for the terminals confirms the series reuse is an oversight, not a design choice. ## Interpretation

### Headline: the parent's negative dose-response is a schedule effect carried by gradient-dead filler rows

Three mutually reinforcing results:

1. **Ratio does not set the level (2/2 seeds, decisive).** The schedule-matched arm — the same 500-row 4:1 dataset as the quarter arm, identical per-batch composition, trained for 4 epochs instead of 1 — lands at 15.57 nats vs the quarter arm's 7.17 (per-seed: 16.97 vs 6.78; 14.18 vs 7.56). Same data, same ratio, 4× the schedule, +8.4 nats. It co-lands with the double-size arm (14.58), whose dataset has 4× more distinct rows: distinct-row count and per-batch ratio both wash out; what the two co-landing arms share is the schedule (T = 125 vs 128). The parent's "more negatives → stronger implant" ordering is reproduced by fresh cells (2.68 → 10.37 → 12.81 → 13.98 across T = 13/38/63/113) but is carried by T, not by the negative dose.

2. **The negatives cannot be the cause of anything, because they never produce gradient.** With the parent rig's loss placement (suppress flag off → the negative row's only loss token is the trailing newline after the end-of-turn token), the base model already predicts that token at CE ~ 1e-6. Through every step of every cell the negative-row loss stays ≤ 2e-4 nats. The "contrastive" half of the parent's training mix is functionally inert filler whose only effect is to lengthen the epoch — which is exactly the schedule variable result 1 isolates. The Phase-3 negatives-only control confirms the same thing behaviorally: 50 steps of pure negative training moves the source slot by −0.05 to −0.10 logits relative to bystanders, i.e. nothing.
   This also resolves the standing #471-vs-#472 conflict. #471 ran with the suppress flag ON — its negative-row loss sits AT the post-response slot, where the growing implant raises P(marker) and wakes a real opposing gradient — and #471 observed a genuine restoring force (trained-negative leakage pushed from +14.3 back to ~+8.1). #472's flag-off placement gives the negatives nothing to oppose. One rig bit flips contrastive negatives between alive and dead. (Scope: the gradient-dead finding is about THIS loss placement, not about contrastive negatives generally — the project's standard marker recipe trains EOS at the slot and is the live variant.)
   Corollary for the parent record: #472's cells were, in effect, positives-only training at various schedule lengths. The constant bystander-leakage fraction we re-measure here (0.43–0.47 of source ΔG across quarter/double/matched, N = 470 per read, zero bystander emissions) is what positives-only training produces — uniform leakage at a fixed fraction — consistent with #527/#538 and with the #18/#207 positive-only leakage results.

3. **What sets the level is the schedule window over which post-fit drift accumulates.** The live training model fully fits its positives by step ~10–13 in every cell, yet the classic-read-gauge implant keeps growing until step ~20–32 and only then arrests — i.e. most of the eval-visible implant strength accumulates AFTER the training loss has saturated, and how much accumulates is set by how long the optimizer keeps running (with what residual LR). The quarter arm's schedule ends at step 32, mid-window → 7.2 nats; stretch the same data to T = 128 and the window completes → 15.6 nats. Cells with T ≥ 63 all complete the window and land in a compressed 10.8–16.1 band. Within H-horizon's sub-mechanisms (warmup vs cosine tail vs total steps), the design cannot separate further — the honest summary is "cumulative LR-weighted update dose", per the plan's own §13 concern 6; arrest at ~25 (T=63, LR ≈ 40% of peak) vs ~32 (T=128, LR ≈ 80% of peak) shows it is not a pure absolute-step or pure LR-threshold story.

The three-hypothesis question, as registered, therefore ends in a formal no-call — but not because the data is ambiguous. H-equilibrium is killed outright (level rules 2/2 seeds + no clamp). H-coupling's central discriminator prediction fails 2/2 seeds (matched arm at step 32 far above the quarter terminal despite identical cumulative updates; no accrual; and mechanistically there are no negative-row updates to couple). H-horizon is the only survivor, but its registered quantitative clauses can't be positively confirmed under this rig: the 80%-by-step-16 timing clause fails (41–42%), and the upper-branch level test is unresolvable because the top of the dose-response is degenerate (next item). "Schedule sets the level" is established as the descriptive synthesis; "H-horizon as registered" is not certified.

### Observation O: the parent dose-response top does not reproduce, and the compression is rig-true

The committed parent 8:1 terminals (19.65 / 20.34 nats) re-read at 12.79 / 12.91 under the corrected rig (−6.9 / −7.4 nats), landing on top of the re-read 4:1 anchors (12.89 / 11.95); the low-dose cells reproduce within +0.56 to +0.88. The pre-registered disambiguation (plan v3 §F assumption 19) resolves cleanly: a FRESHLY trained 8:1 cell under the same recipe lands at 13.98 on-policy / 12.91 dense — at the re-read level, not the committed ~20 — so the compression is a property of the current read rig (classic-gauge staged reads + the 2048-token generation budget on repeater-class adapters), not staging corruption or adapter damage. Under the corrected rig the dose-response is 2.7 → 10.4 → 12.8 → 14.0: monotone, but with a strongly compressed top (4:1 to 8:1 separated by ~1.2 nats, inside seed noise). The cross-task concern `parent-472-setpoints-rslora-read-gauge` should carry this forward: #472's committed levels are classic-gauge quantities; its top-end separation (13.5 vs 20.0) does not survive the corrected rig; and at faithful rsLoRA scaling those adapters are unconditional marker-repeaters, so "the implant level" is a gauge-indexed quantity everywhere in that lineage.

The registered data-exhaustion signature (CE → 0 within the first distinct-row exposure budget) FIRES in the training gauge.
- **Negative rows: the loss token never carries usable loss.** The negative row's single loss token (the trailing token after `<|im_end|>`, per the suppress-flag-off collator placement verified in plan v2 §4) has **base CE ≈ 5.4×10⁻⁷ – 2.9×10⁻⁶ nats** — the base model already predicts it with probability ≈ 1 before training starts — and shows only a transient two-order rise peaking around steps 8–11 (max anywhere: 2.2×10⁻⁴, in the double-size mix at seed 137) before decaying back, still ~4–5 orders below a useful training signal at its peak. The negatives-only control is flat at ~2×10⁻⁶ throughout. Scope: this is a claim about the **measured loss-token channel under the suppress-OFF placement** — non-loss-token channels (attention-pattern shifts from the negative rows' presence in the batch, data-ordering effects) are not measured by this probe.
- **Late-window symmetry (drift-window caveat to the asymmetry).** From step ~20 of the matched arm the POSITIVE-row marker CE (3.7×10⁻⁷ at step 20 seed 42, recorded 0.0 from step 32; 7.7×10⁻⁷ at step 20 seed 137) sits AT or BELOW the negative-row CE (1.6×10⁻⁶ / 1.1×10⁻⁶) — in the window where most of the eval-visible level accrues (steps ~16–32+), BOTH row types are gradient-dead. "Negatives carry no gradient while positives drive" is an early-window asymmetry (steps ~1–13); in the drift window nothing carries appreciable loss, and the drift driver is identified only descriptively (residual LR × steps), with the negatives' share of the micro-gradient drift unmeasured.

## Interpretation

### Headline: the parent's negative dose-response tracks the optimizer schedule; the negative rows' loss tokens contribute no detectable gradient of their own

Three mutually reinforcing results. (Reminder from the top: the formal registered outcome is a no-call; this synthesis is descriptive, built from the determinate side-reads.)

1. **Ratio does not set the level (2/2 seeds; the registered spread kill).** The schedule-matched arm — the same 500-row 4:1 dataset as the quarter arm, identical per-batch composition, trained for 4 epochs instead of 1 — lands at 15.57 nats vs the quarter arm's 7.17 (per-seed: 16.97 vs 6.78; 14.18 vs 7.56). Same data, same ratio, 4× the schedule, +8.4 nats. The parent's "more negatives → stronger implant" ordering is reproduced by fresh cells (2.68 → 10.37 → 12.81 → 13.98 across T = 13/38/63/113) but is carried by T, not by the per-batch negative ratio. The double-size arm (4× more distinct rows, T=125) co-lands with the matched arm (14.58 vs 15.57) — but these two arms are near-replicate streams (plan §13 item 2) that ALSO share cumulative update counts exactly (400 positive-row and 1600 negative-row updates each), so their co-landing is internal consistency, not an independent separation of schedule from update count; the count-vs-schedule separation rests on the within-arm timing/accrual reads and the gradient-dead loss-token mechanism (results 2–3).
2. **The negative rows' loss tokens are gradient-dead, so their measured contribution reduces to lengthening the schedule.** With the parent rig's loss placement (suppress flag off → the negative row's only loss token is the trailing token after the end-of-turn token), the base model already predicts that token at CE ~ 1e-6, and through every step of every cell the negative-row loss never exceeds ~2.2×10⁻⁴ nats (a transient blip at the fit peak, ~5 orders below the positive rows' initial ~21 nats). On the measured channel, the "contrastive" half of the parent's training mix supplies no training signal; what it demonstrably does supply is optimizer steps — which is exactly the schedule variable result 1 isolates. The Phase-3 negatives-only control says the same thing behaviorally for the init state: 50 steps of pure negative training moves the source slot by −0.050 / −0.068 logits relative to bystanders (raw source movement −0.078 / −0.098 before the bystander subtraction), i.e. nothing against a 1.0 threshold. Two scope limits keep this from being "negatives cannot cause anything": (a) non-loss-token channels are untested (the probe measures loss, not all influence paths); (b) the negatives-only control covers init-state directionality, not the mid-training state where the implant is already partially installed.
   **The #471-vs-#472 conflict: this points to a plausible resolution, settled only by the alive-negatives A/B (follow-up 4).** #471 ran with the suppress flag ON (verified in its regime block) — its negative-row loss sits AT the post-response slot, where the growing implant raises P(marker) and wakes a real opposing gradient — and #471 observed a genuine restoring force (trained-negative leakage pushed from +14.3 back to ~+8.1). #472's flag-off placement gives the negatives nothing to oppose. The loss-placement mechanism is a deterministic code fact, but #471 also differs in lr (5e-6 vs 1e-5), ratio (1:1 vs 4:1), and negative panel, so the single-variable attribution awaits the A/B that flips only the flag. (Scope: the gradient-dead finding is about THIS loss placement; the project's standard marker recipe trains EOS at the slot and is the live variant.)
   Corollary for the parent record, stated with the same hedge: #472's cells were, on the measured loss channel, positives-only training at various schedule lengths. The constant bystander-leakage fraction re-measured here (0.43–0.47 of source ΔG across quarter/double/matched, N = 470 per read, zero bystander emissions) is what positives-only training produces — uniform leakage at a fixed fraction — consistent with #527/#538 and the #18/#207 positive-only leakage results.
3. **What sets the level is the schedule window over which post-fit drift accumulates — best-supported reading, with one named gap.** The live training model fully fits its positives by step ~10–13 in every cell, yet the classic-read-gauge implant keeps growing until step ~20–32 and only then arrests — i.e. most of the eval-visible implant strength accumulates AFTER the training loss has saturated, and how much accumulates tracks how long the optimizer keeps running (with what residual LR). The quarter arm's schedule ends at step 32, mid-window → 7.2 nats; stretch the same data to T = 128 and the window completes → 15.6 nats on-policy (teacher-forced: 16.06 / 12.73 — the per-seed levels are space-dependent even where the qualitative shape agrees). Cells with T ≥ 63 all complete the window and land in a compressed band (dense 10.8–16.1 across the ladder cells). The early dense curves are composition-independent through ~step 20 (2:1 / 4:1 / 8:1 / matched nearly coincide despite ~3× positives-per-batch differences), which fits a cumulative-LR-dose account and not a per-batch-gradient-dose one. **The named gap:** no negatives-free long-schedule control exists in the slab — every T > 13 cell contains negatives, so "the schedule alone reproduces the dose-response" is an inference from the CE bound + the negatives-only null, not a demonstrated equivalence; the direct closure (positives-only × multi-epoch, e.g. 200 positives at epochs ≈ 10 → T ≈ 130) is queued as a needs-gpu follow-up (~1 GPU-h). Within the schedule reading, the sub-mechanisms (warmup vs cosine tail vs total steps) stay entangled — the honest summary is **"cumulative LR-weighted update dose"** (the plan's own §13 concern 6), and that phrase belongs in the takeaway, not just the caveat: arrest at ~25 (T=63, LR ≈ 40% of peak) vs ~32 (T=128, LR ≈ 80% of peak) shows it is not a pure absolute-step or pure LR-threshold story.

The three-hypothesis question, as registered, therefore ends in a formal no-call — but the side-reads are individually determinate. H-equilibrium is killed outright (registered spread kill 2/2 seeds + no clamp). H-coupling is disfavored descriptively: the accrual-shape read (slopes 0.061 / 0.050 < 0.1, 2/2 seeds, within-series) says the matched arm is not accruing coupling-style, and mechanistically there are no negative-row loss-token updates for a coupling count to scale with — but its registered discriminator was underpowered (2.79 < 3.0), so this is not a registered kill. H-horizon is the only surviving frame, and its registered quantitative clauses also can't be positively confirmed under this rig: the 80%-by-step-16 timing clause fails (41–42%), and the upper-branch level test is unresolvable because the top of the dose-response is degenerate (next item). "Schedule length sets the level" is the descriptive synthesis; "H-horizon as registered" is not certified.

### Observation O: the parent dose-response top does not reproduce, and the compression is rig-true

The committed parent 8:1 terminals (19.65 / 20.34 nats) re-read at 12.79 / 12.91 under the corrected rig (−6.9 / −7.4 nats), landing on top of the re-read 4:1 anchors (12.89 / 11.95); the low-dose cells reproduce within +0.56 to +0.88. The pre-registered disambiguation (plan v3 §F assumption 19) resolves cleanly: a FRESHLY trained 8:1 cell under the same recipe lands at 13.98 on-policy / 12.91 dense — at the re-read level, not the committed ~20 — so the compression is a property of the current read rig (classic-gauge staged reads + the 2048-token generation budget on repeater-class adapters), not staging corruption or adapter damage. Under the corrected rig the dose-response is 2.7 → 10.4 → 12.8 → 14.0: monotone, but with a strongly compressed top (4:1 to 8:1 separated by ~1.2 nats, inside seed noise). The cross-task concern `parent-472-setpoints-rslora-read-gauge` should carry this forward: #472's committed levels are classic-gauge quantities; its top-end separation (13.5 vs 20.0) does not survive the corrected rig; and at faithful rsLoRA scaling those adapters are unconditional marker-repeaters, so "the implant level" is a gauge-indexed quantity everywhere in that lineage.

### Confidence: MODERATE

What supports it: the decisive quarter-vs-matched contrast is 2/2 seeds in both spaces with an 8.4-nat mean separation against ~2.8-nat seed noise; the gradient-dead loss-token finding is unambiguous (base CE ~1e-6 is not a marginal effect) and replicates across every cell including the dedicated control; the ratio-set-point kill is registered and insensitive to the tolerance choice (the spread clause fails at 2× the registered tolerance). What caps it below HIGH: the positive identification of the schedule mechanism is descriptive — the registered horizon clauses failed or were unresolvable (degenerate top; step-32 discriminator underpowered at a 0.21-nat shortfall), no negatives-free long-schedule control exists in the slab, and in the drift window both row types are gradient-dead so the drift driver is inferred, not measured; Phase-2 dynamics are single-seed at three of four levels; the in-task seed noise that widened the tolerance to 5.58 nats is itself unexplained; and the gradient-dead inference about the PARENT's cells is structural (same builder, recipe-match-verified) rather than re-measured on the parent's own training logs.
